end.summary:
Harsh discussed real-life uses of coordinate geometry, including locating places on a map.
They considered using a stationery shop for the homework example and diagram.
They identified (-3, 2) as Quadrant II after correction.
They repeatedly treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point; this was not corrected later.
They stated that the origin is (0, 0), with no movement, and where the axes meet.
end.parentNote: Harsh practised connecting coordinate geometry to map locations and choosing a stationery shop for a real-life example. They used the signs of coordinates to identify Quadrant II for (-3, 2), after first choosing Quadrant IV. A mix-up remained: (3, 2) and (2, 3) were treated as the same point and were not corrected later in the lesson. At home, have them plot both points on one grid and compare their positions.
